classification_basis: variable rectangular flat-pad footprints fitted to one horizontal platform plane using known ground-support provenance; PHM steel deck anchors Medium; district capacity remains a later aggregation concept

small.classification_rule: qualifies if any configured flat-pad footprint in this class fits; highest supported class wins; within class prefer largest area then lowest perimeter/mean clearance

medium.intent: substantial dedicated flat pad; PHM steel deck is the calibration anchor
medium.classification_rule: qualifies if any configured flat-pad footprint in this class fits; highest supported class wins; within class prefer largest area then lowest perimeter/mean clearance

large.intent: large single flat industrial pad; district growth may combine several pads
large.classification_rule: qualifies if any configured flat-pad footprint in this class fits; highest supported class wins; within class prefer largest area then lowest perimeter/mean clearance

very_large.intent: exceptionally broad single flat industrial pad; not the same as regional district capacity
very_large.classification_rule: qualifies if any configured flat-pad footprint in this class fits; highest supported class wins; within class prefer largest area then lowest perimeter/mean clearance

workable.interpretation: placement zone with some directional constraint

poor.interpretation: highly elongated placement zone; rectangle location is more informative than region shape

notes: V8 recalibrates physical flat-pad classes separately from later district-capacity aggregation: Small short side >=8 foundations, Medium >=12 (PHM 12x26 steel deck anchor), Large >=20, Very Large >=32.
Size-class hotkeys in the viewer are S/M/L/V; numeric 3 is intentionally not used because VTK reserves it for stereo/CrystalEyes display mode.

V8 lowers minimum known-ground footprint coverage to 80%, matching the PHM steel-deck calibration where ~81% of foundation centers resolve to landscape/fill and the remainder is cliff/overhead ambiguity.
Clearance variants extend through 32/64 m for diagnostic exploration; these loose settings are not recommended grounded-build defaults, but they expose the expected Large/Very Large progression.
V7 replaces one fixed square/rectangle per size class with an editable footprint family. Size class describes capacity band, not a required aspect ratio.
Viewer rectangle dimensions are always physical foundation dimensions: width_foundations * 8 m and length_foundations * 8 m, independent of analysis resolution.
The contextual suitability fill is emitted from the union of qualifying footprint coverage, while center-membership remains available for region identity/debugging.
Every qualifying rectangle is one flat horizontal platform. Its Z is fitted to the highest known ground-support cell in the footprint.

Landscape (provenance 1) and fill (3) are treated as ground support. Cliff surfaces (4/5) are not assumed to be ground because the 2.5D heightfield may be showing an overhead rock or natural bridge instead of the usable floor beneath.

A footprint may contain a limited fraction of cliff-only/unknown ground cells. Defaults require at least 85% known ground across the footprint and 75% around the perimeter; ambiguity is emitted as a metric rather than silently interpreted.
At 16 m working resolution each support cell uses the median of its underlying known-ground samples. Decrease working resolution to make smaller terrain details matter.

For a tolerance T, the lowest no-penetration platform is fitted at the highest known ground cell and known-ground maximum clearance must also be <= T. At T=4 m this approximates a 4 m foundation remaining terrain-supported rather than visibly floating.

The PHM_steel_deck_502094 calibration fixture is a 221-foundation flat 4 m deck. On known landscape/fill centers its top is ~3.0 m above terrain median, 3.8 m at p95; 42 centers coincide with cliff/overhead top-surface provenance and are kept separate from support clearance.
The irregular region is only the connected zone of qualifying rectangle centers. Emitted rectangles and fitted platform elevations are the primary planning geometry.
build_surfaces_v5 remains available as the all-top-surface plane-fit baseline; v4 and v3 remain alternate analyses.
V6 remains available as the single-reference-footprint baseline.
